newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium offers troops to train Zaire peacekeepers.
newsitem.headline: Belgium offers troops to train Zaire peacekeepers.

text.p: Belgium said on Wednesday it was ready to send troops to Africa to train local forces for an eventual United Nations peacekeeping force in eastern Zaire.
"Belgian military units could leave quickly for African countries that ask for our assistance in getting ready their peacekeeping forces," a Belgian Foreign Ministry spokesman told a news conference.

He reiterated, however, that Belgium would not take part directly in a UN force in Zaire, Rwanda or Burundi -- which are former Belgian colonies or protectorates and where it has lost troops in past interventions.

Belgium has already sent four military C-130 Hercules cargo aircraft to Uganda to help lift aid to refugees fleeing fighting between ethnic Tutsis and Hutus in Zaire's eastern Kivu region. It has also earmarked 300 million Belgian francs ($10 million) for aid agencies working in the area.
The spokesman said Belgium was ready to fly aid directly to Zaire if and when Zaire's government, which has in recent years had a frosty relationship with its former ruler, gave its permission.
"A part of Zaire's population has fallen victim to the present crisis," he said.
He said flights could go to Kinshasa or Kisangani airports. He did not have details of the amount of aid that could be available.

The spokesman said Belgium would use its position as chairman of a meeting of Western European Union Defence and Foreign Ministers next week to discuss how the WEU could help transport an intervention force and aid to eastern Zaire.
Belgium has proposed the WEU get involved in African peacekeeping operations ever since mainly Hutu militias massacred hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Tutsis in 1994.
